info.title: IronForge API
info.description: IronForge is a self-hosted Git platform written in Rust. This API provides repository management, issue tracking, pull requests, CI/CD pipelines, wiki, LFS, webhooks, and more.

get.summary:
Download an LFS object: GET /repos/:owner/:name/lfs/objects/:oid
Streams the object, decompressing on the fly if compressed.
For compressed objects, uses spawn_blocking + channel for streaming
zstd decompression without blocking the async runtime.

put.summary:
Upload an LFS object: PUT /repos/:owner/:name/lfs/objects/:oid
Streams the request body directly to a temp file, then stream-compresses
it with zstd — never buffers the entire object in memory.

get.description:
Public profile lookup. The CLI resolves assignee names to ids with it
(there is no by-name route equivalent otherwise).

client_request_id.description: Client-chosen idempotency key, unique per acting session or user.

depends_on_task_id.description: The task this task waits for (same repository).

expected_graph_version.description: The graph version last read from `GET .../dependencies` (0 = no edge yet).

client_request_id.description: Idempotency key, unique per adding session or user.

commit_sha.description: Full 40/64-digit commit id that exists in the target repository now.

target_repo_id.description: Stable id of the target repository (not its name).

target_task_id.description: A collaboration task of the target repository.

AddTimeRequest.description: Request body for adding a time entry.

AiTreeEntry.description: One entry of the file tree. `path` is relative to the repository root.

commit.description: Commit the ref resolved to; `None` for a repository without commits.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` to fetch the next page.

ref.description: The ref as requested (or the default branch).

truncated.description: More entries exist beyond this page.

acknowledged_context_hash.description: `context_hash` of the question as read; proves the context was seen.

body.description: Up to 16 KiB; required unless the question has options.

expected_version.description: The question `version` the caller last saw.

option_id.description: Required when the question has options.

mfa_required.description: Whether MFA verification is still required

api_capabilities.description: Versioned, instance-wide REST behaviors; unknown names may be ignored.

build_commit.description: Source commit supplied at build time, or null when unavailable.

build_dirty.description: True for a modified checkout; null when the build source is unknown.

contract_version.description: `major.minor`. Same major = compatible; a higher minor only adds optional things.

mcp_tools.description: MCP tools adapting the capability (empty when REST-only).

requires.description:
What a caller needs: any of `account`, `repo_collab_read`, `repo_write`,
`session_credentials`, `repo_admin`, `site_admin`. Clients ignore names they do not know
but must not assume an unknown requirement is satisfied.

status.description: `stable` | `experimental`. Clients treat an unknown value as `experimental`.

client_change_id.description: Idempotency key, unique per writing session or user.

replacement_decision_id.description:
Required for `superseded`, forbidden for `revoked`. A decision of the
same task recorded after the one it replaces.

CodeSearchResult.description: Code search result for AI API

id.description: Keep an existing condition's identity by sending its id; omit to add one.

base_sha.description: Full commit ids that exist in this repository (existence only).

org.description: Organization name — if provided, create repo under this org

display_name.description: Self-reported label, 1–80 characters. Duplicates are allowed.

branch.description: Declared working branch (not checked against Git).

repos.description:

client_package_id.description: Idempotency key, unique per author session or user.

hint.description: One sentence on what to do next, for a client that cannot guess.

reason.description:
Stable, finer-grained cause inside `code` (e.g. `REF_ADVANCED` under
`CONFLICT`). Clients branch on this instead of parsing `message`. Present
only on the errors that have one.

request_id.description: Request ID (injected by request-id middleware for error responses).

retryable.description: Whether repeating the request after re-reading state can succeed.

kind.description: `pipeline` (a pipeline id of this repository), `commit`, `url` or `note`.

client_task_id.description: Idempotency key, unique per creating session.

notes.description: Free text appended to the task description (up to 4 KiB).

owner_session_id.description: A live session of this repository; omit for an unowned task.

params.description: Values for the title pattern's placeholders, exactly those names.

rules_ref.description:
Optional branch, tag or commit. When given, the commit it resolves to now
is recorded on the task as `rules_commit` (O01); an unresolvable ref is a

version.description: Pin this version; default the latest at the time of the request.

observed_version.description: The `object_version` that was read; not newer than the record's current one.

consistency with the register endpoint, which uses `username`.

last_read_seq.description: Highest message `seq` the session has processed.

The session's watermark after the call. Monotonic: a lower request leaves
it unchanged, so `last_read_seq: 0` reads the current value.

tool_count.description: Number of `collab_*` tools. The authoritative list is MCP `tools/list`.

transports.description: Only `stdio` exists; there is no HTTP/SSE MCP endpoint.

next_after_seq.description: Use as the next `after_seq`; equals the request's value on an empty page.

has_prev.description: Whether there is a previous page.

settings_version.description: Opaque version of the editable settings, present on repository reads.

Non-negative decimal, greater than zero, at most 18 integer and 6

unit.description:
